steps.title: Import Vue and ref from vue
steps.instruction: Import Vue and the ref function from the 'vue' package.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in Vue and ref from the vue module.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Vue framework and ref function are imported and available for use.
successCriteria: Vue and ref are imported from 'vue'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported Vue and ref. These are essential for creating reactive components in Vue.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're importing both Vue and ref from the 'vue' package.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check your import statement. It should import both Vue and ref from the 'vue' package.

steps.title: Create the useClickOutside composable function
steps.instruction: Define a function called useClickOutside that takes a callback parameter.
steps.hint: Start by writing a function declaration or arrow function with the name useClickOutside and one parameter.
steps.seedCode:
// Import Vue and ref from 'vue'

// Define the useClickOutside function here
steps.expectedOutcome: A useClickOutside function is defined with a callback parameter.
successCriteria: The useClickOutside function is defined and accepts a callback parameter.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the useClickOutside composable function with a callback parameter.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've defined a function named useClickOutside that accepts a callback parameter.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function definition is missing or incorrect. Define a function called useClickOutside that takes a callback parameter.

steps.title: Initialize a ref for the target element
steps.instruction: Inside the useClickOutside function, create a ref called elementRef with null as its initial value.
steps.hint: Use the ref function imported from Vue to create a reactive reference that can store a DOM element.
steps.analogousExample:
// Creating a ref to store an element
const elementRef = ref(null);
steps.expectedOutcome: The useClickOutside function now contains a ref called elementRef initialized to null.
successCriteria: elementRef is declared inside useClickOutside using ref(null).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created a reactive reference to store the DOM element we'll monitor for outside clicks.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're using the ref function to create elementRef with null as the initial value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The step requires creating a ref called elementRef inside the useClickOutside function. Check that you're using the ref function correctly.

steps.title: Define the click handler function
steps.instruction: Inside the useClickOutside function, define a function named handleClick that takes an event parameter.
steps.hint: You can use either a function declaration or arrow function syntax. The function should be defined inside useClickOutside but before the return statement.
steps.expectedOutcome: The useClickOutside function now contains a handleClick function that will process click events.
successCriteria: A function named handleClick is defined inside useClickOutside and accepts an event parameter.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've defined the click handler function. This function will check whether clicks occur outside our target element.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've defined a function named handleClick that takes an event parameter inside the useClickOutside function.
steps.feedbackWrong: The handleClick function isn't properly defined. Check that you've created a function named handleClick with an event parameter inside useClickOutside.

steps.title: Implement click outside logic in handler
steps.instruction: Inside the handleClick function, add logic to check if elementRef.value exists and if the click event target is outside that element, then call a callback function.
steps.hint: You can use the contains method on the DOM element to check if the clicked target is inside elementRef.value. If it's outside, you should call a callback function (you'll pass this callback later).
steps.expectedOutcome: The handleClick function now contains logic to detect clicks outside the target element and will trigger a callback when that happens.
successCriteria: The handleClick function checks if elementRef.value exists and uses contains to verify the click target is outside it, then calls a callback function.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully implemented the click detection logic. The handler now checks if clicks occur outside the target element.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your logic includes both the existence check for elementRef.value and the contains check for the event target.
steps.feedbackWrong: The click detection logic isn't quite right. Remember to check if elementRef.value exists and use contains to see if the click target is outside that element.

steps.title: Add event listener setup
steps.instruction: Inside the useClickOutside function, add an event listener to the document that calls handleClick when the component mounts.
steps.hint: Use the document.addEventListener method with 'click' as the event type and handleClick as the callback.
steps.expectedOutcome: The useClickOutside function now sets up a click event listener on the document that will trigger the handleClick function.
successCriteria: The useClickOutside function includes document.addEventListener('click', handleClick) inside its body.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the event listener setup. This will detect all clicks on the document.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're adding the event listener inside the useClickOutside function body.
steps.feedbackWrong: The event listener setup is missing. Add document.addEventListener('click', handleClick) inside the useClickOutside function.

steps.title: Add cleanup for event listener
steps.instruction: Inside the useClickOutside function, return a cleanup function that removes the click event listener from the document.
steps.hint: Return a function that calls document.removeEventListener with the same event type and handler as the setup.
steps.expectedOutcome: The useClickOutside function now returns a cleanup function that will remove the click event listener when called.
successCriteria: A cleanup function is returned from useClickOutside that calls document.removeEventListener with 'click' and handleClick.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added the cleanup function to prevent memory leaks by removing the event listener.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're returning a function that removes the click event listener with the same handler.
steps.feedbackWrong: The cleanup function is missing or incorrect. Return a function that calls document.removeEventListener('click', handleClick).

steps.title: Create the main App component
steps.instruction: Create a Vue component named App with a setup function that returns an empty template.
steps.hint: In Vue, you can define a component using a function that returns an object with a setup method.
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component is defined with a setup function that returns an empty template.
successCriteria: App component is created with a setup function that returns a render function.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the main App component structure.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the App component has a setup function that returns a render function.
steps.feedbackWrong: The App component is not properly defined. Check the structure of Vue components.

steps.title: Initialize state for modal visibility
steps.instruction: Inside the App component's setup function, create a reactive ref called 'isModalOpen' with an initial value of false.
steps.hint: Use the 'ref' function imported earlier to create reactive state. Initialize it with 'false'.
steps.analogousExample:
// Creating reactive state for visibility
const isVisible = ref(false);
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component will have reactive state to track whether a modal should be open or closed.
successCriteria: The App component contains a ref named 'isModalOpen' initialized to false.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created reactive state to control modal visibility.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've created a ref called 'isModalOpen' with an initial value of false inside the App component.
steps.feedbackWrong: The state initialization is missing or incorrect. Create a ref called 'isModalOpen' with an initial value of false inside the App component.

steps.title: Use the click outside composable
steps.instruction: Inside the App component, call the useClickOutside composable and destructure its returned elementRef. Pass a callback function that sets isModalOpen to false when called.
steps.hint: Call useClickOutside with a callback that updates the state. The composable returns an object containing elementRef.
steps.expectedOutcome: The useClickOutside composable is integrated into the App component, with elementRef destructured and a callback provided to handle outside clicks.
successCriteria: useClickOutside is called with a callback that sets isModalOpen to false, and elementRef is destructured from its return value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully integrated the useClickOutside composable with the App component.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're calling useClickOutside with a callback and destructuring elementRef from its return value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The composable isn't properly integrated. Review how to call useClickOutside and destructure its return value.

steps.title: Create the modal structure
steps.instruction: In the App component's return object, add a template property that returns a div for the modal. Use v-if="isModalOpen" to conditionally render it and bind elementRef to the modal div using ref="elementRef".
steps.hint: The template should be a function that returns the modal structure. Remember to bind the ref to the modal div so useClickOutside can detect clicks outside it.
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component now returns a template with a modal div that conditionally renders based on isModalOpen and has elementRef bound to it.
successCriteria: The return object has a template property containing a modal div with v-if="isModalOpen" and ref="elementRef" attributes.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the modal structure with conditional rendering and ref binding.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the template property returns a modal div with both v-if="isModalOpen" and ref="elementRef" attributes.
steps.feedbackWrong: The modal structure is missing or incomplete. The template should include a div with v-if="isModalOpen" and ref="elementRef".

steps.title: Add toggle button and complete the component
steps.instruction: Add a button inside the template that toggles the isModalOpen state when clicked, and return the template from the App component.
steps.hint: Use @click to call a function that changes isModalOpen.value. The button should be placed inside the template structure.
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component will have a button that toggles modal visibility and a complete template structure.
successCriteria: Button with @click handler that toggles isModalOpen is added, and template property returns the complete component structure.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the toggle button and completed the component structure.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you've added both the button with @click handler and the template property.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button or template structure is missing. Check that you've added a button with @click that toggles isModalOpen and returned the template from the App component.
